seoTitle: Cancel & Delete Google Workspace Without Losing Data
metaDescription: Ending your Google Workspace trial or subscription? Learn how to find billing in the Admin Console, cancel correctly, and preserve your data first.
intro: Canceling a Google Workspace subscription without an unexpected charge or lost data takes a bit of care, especially since the cancellation control sits a few clicks deep in the Admin Console instead of on the main dashboard. This guide follows that path: from the Admin Console home, into Billing, to the menu where Cancel subscription lives, and what to sort out with your data and billing plan before you click it.
prerequisites: Super Admin or Billing Admin access to the Google Workspace account. A standard user role can't reach the Billing pages.
costNote: Canceling itself doesn't cost anything, but what happens to your existing charges depends on the plan type. A Flexible plan stops billing once the cancellation takes effect, charged only for the days used that cycle. An Annual or Fixed-Term plan bills you for the remaining balance of the committed term even though you're canceling early. Check which plan type is on the account in Billing before assuming cancellation stops all charges.

steps.heading: Start from the Admin Console home
steps.body: Sign in to admin.google.com with your administrator account. The home screen's "Manage Workspace" section shows two cards relevant here: Users, for managing accounts, and Billing, which displays your paid service start date and links for Manage subscriptions, Payment accounts, and Buy or upgrade. This is also where Google surfaces "Recommendations for getting started" prompts, which are safe to ignore if you're here to wind the account down instead of set it up further.

image.caption: The Admin Console home screen. The Billing card shows your paid service start date with a direct Manage subscriptions link.

steps.heading: Open Manage subscriptions under Billing
steps.body: Click Manage subscriptions from the Billing card, or navigate to Billing in the left sidebar and select Subscriptions directly. This lands you on the page listing your active Google Workspace plan along with its billing history, the same place to check what you were charged and when your current cycle ends. It's also where the plan type shows up (Flexible versus Annual or Fixed-Term), which matters for what canceling costs; see the note above.

steps.heading: Open the subscription's action menu
steps.body: On the subscription itself, a menu (usually reached via a kebab or options icon next to the plan) expands into four choices: Add payment method, View payment settings, Downgrade, and Cancel subscription, each with its own icon. Downgrade sits directly above Cancel subscription, worth noticing: if the actual goal is fewer features or lower cost instead of shutting everything down, Downgrade is the less drastic option one click above the one you might have come here for.

image.caption: The subscription's action menu, with Cancel subscription listed below Add payment method, View payment settings, and Downgrade.

steps.heading: Export your data before you confirm cancellation
steps.body: Google's own documentation for canceling Google Workspace describes losing access to core services like Gmail and Calendar once the cancellation takes effect, ahead of a separate, longer window (documented as up to 90 days for verified subscriptions) before the account's data is permanently deleted. Treat that window as a courtesy, not a plan: export what you need before you confirm the cancellation, not after. Google Takeout, at takeout.google.com, downloads an archive of Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and other Google service data tied to an account. Run it for every user on the Workspace, not just the administrator's own account.

steps.heading: Confirm the cancellation and check for lingering costs
steps.body: Selecting Cancel subscription from the menu opens a confirmation flow where Google states what happens next, and this is where the plan-type distinction from the costNote above plays out for real: a Flexible plan stops charging once you confirm, while an Annual or Fixed-Term plan can bill the remaining contract balance in that same step. After confirming, go back to Billing and Payment accounts and check that no other add-ons or third-party subscriptions billed through the Workspace account are still active, since those don't automatically cancel alongside the core Workspace plan and can keep charging after everything looks shut down.

steps.heading: Decide what happens to the domain and remaining users
steps.body: If a custom domain was purchased or managed through Google Workspace, canceling the subscription doesn't automatically release or transfer it. That needs handling separately, either by transferring the domain elsewhere or confirming its own renewal status independently of the Workspace plan. Check for any locked user accounts or extra licenses still counted against the billing before considering the cancellation fully wrapped up, since an overlooked license is one of the more common ways people end up surprised by a final invoice.

troubleshooting.problem: Billed again after canceling, even though the subscription shows canceled
troubleshooting.cause: The account is on an Annual or Fixed-Term plan. Google bills for the remaining contract balance at cancellation instead of simply stopping charges.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the plan type in Billing before canceling. If it's Fixed-Term, that final charge is expected and documented, not a billing error.

troubleshooting.problem: A free trial silently converts into a paid subscription
troubleshooting.cause: Google's own free-trial documentation states that once a payment method is added, the paid subscription starts automatically the moment the trial ends, with no extra confirmation step.
troubleshooting.fix: Go to Billing and Subscriptions and cancel before the trial's end date if a paid plan isn't wanted yet.

troubleshooting.problem: Emails or Drive files can't be recovered after cancellation
troubleshooting.cause: Access to core services can end as soon as the cancellation takes effect, ahead of the longer data-deletion window Google documents separately.
troubleshooting.fix: Run Google Takeout for every user before confirming cancellation. Don't wait for the deletion window as a backup plan.

faq.question: Will I be charged again if I cancel my subscription?
faq.answer: It depends on the plan type. A Flexible plan stops billing once cancellation takes effect, charged only for days used. An Annual or Fixed-Term plan bills the remaining balance of the committed term, so canceling early doesn't erase that cost. Check Billing to see which type is on the account.

faq.question: Can I get my emails back after canceling Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Access to core services can end as soon as cancellation takes effect, well before Google's documented data-deletion window closes, which is why exporting emails, Drive files, and other data through Google Takeout before finalizing cancellation matters.

faq.question: Does canceling during a free trial still require these steps?
faq.answer: Yes. Ending a trial goes through the same Billing, Subscriptions, Cancel Subscription path in the Admin Console. It matters especially if a payment method was already added, since Google's documentation confirms the paid plan starts automatically the moment the trial ends unless it's canceled first.

faq.question: What's the difference between Downgrade and Cancel subscription?
faq.answer: Downgrade moves the account to a lower-cost or lower-feature plan while keeping the subscription active; Cancel subscription ends it. Both options sit in the same menu, so check Downgrade first if the goal is only to reduce cost.

faq.question: What happens to my custom domain after canceling?
faq.answer: It isn't automatically released or transferred. The domain's renewal or transfer has to be handled separately from the Workspace subscription itself.

verifiedNote: Click path and screenshots come from an Admin Console walkthrough on a live Workspace account. The billing behavior, data-access timing, and free-trial conversion rules were checked against Google Workspace's own Help Center in September 2026. That check corrected this guide's earlier claim that a canceled plan simply 'stays active through the end of the billing period': Google documents two different outcomes depending on whether the plan is Flexible or Annual/Fixed-Term, and only the Flexible case works that way.
